events.title: Jonah's call and flight to Tarshish
events.description: God calls Jonah to preach judgment against Nineveh, the great Assyrian city. But Jonah flees from the Lord's presence and boards a ship bound for Tarshish, in the opposite direction of Nineveh.

events.title: The storm and Jonah is thrown into the sea
events.description: The Lord sends a violent storm over the sea. The sailors cast lots, and the lot falls on Jonah. He admits that the storm is caused by his flight from God and asks them to throw him into the sea. When they do, the sea becomes calm.

events.title: Jonah in the Great Fish
events.description: The Lord sends a great fish that swallows Jonah. For three days and three nights he is in the belly of the fish, where he prays a prayer for deliverance and thanks to God. The fish then vomits him onto dry land.

events.title: Jonah Preaches in Nineveh
events.description: God's word comes to Jonah a second time, and this time he obeys. He enters the great city of Nineveh and proclaims that the city will be destroyed in forty days.

events.title: Nineveh's Repentance
events.description: The people of Nineveh believe God's message. The king himself steps down from his throne, puts on sackcloth, and commands fasting and repentance for the whole city. God sees their repentance and spares the city from destruction.

events.title: Jonah's Anger and God's Lesson
events.description: Jonah becomes angry because God spares Nineveh, complaining that he knew God was gracious and merciful. God causes a plant to grow up to give Jonah shade, but then sends a worm to destroy it. God uses Jonah's grief over the plant as a lesson: Should not God have compassion for Nineveh with its more than 120,000 people?
